# asl verdicts over the over-acceptance probe corpus. GENERATED by
# scripts/mint_over_acceptance_verdicts.sh. Do not hand-edit.
#
# VERDICTS ONLY, NEVER BYTES. Most probes here are supposed to fail, and a
# failing asl run's byte column is an artifact: an error stops asl's pass
# loop, so forward references stay at their pass-1 placeholder and the
# listing prints them looking complete. Reading only accept-or-refuse and
# the diagnostic text is what makes a corpus of failing files a safe
# measurement. See docs/superpowers/notes/asl-reference/asl_ref.sh.
#
# IDENTITY IS THE DIGEST. Seven asl paths on this machine execute under
# four distinct digests and every one prints the banner below, so the
# banner discriminates nothing and is human context only.
# asl-md5     61e672562465725a8c102288a7da9098
# asl-banner  Macro Assembler 1.42 Beta [Bld 212]|(x86_64-unknown-linux)|
#
# diag is asl_diag_state's classification of the listing footer.
# INCOMPLETE means asl refused to start a later pass, so the diagnostics
# that pass would have raised were never looked for: the message column
# for such a row is the FIRST thing asl noticed, not the only thing wrong.
#
